Fire! Your group of Neanderthals must now endure Mother Nature and work together to keep the fire going long enough to learn its mysterious powers and destructive capabilities. You have 14 days to uncover its secrets before a massive flood drowns the valley and extinguishes humanity’s one chance at becoming the apex predator and escaping extinction. Don't Let It Die is a cooperative survival game based on early humanity's struggles to cement their place at the top of the food chain. You will gather resources & food, fight deadly predators, and learn the mysteries of fire. Your task is a difficult one, but no matter what happens, remember: you and the fire must survive... Your tribe consists of 4 characters, all taking turns to search for resources, fight off dangerous animals, unlock new discoveries, and working together to keep the fire alive! Designed from the ground up to offer a re-playable, interactive, strategic cooperative experience for 1-4 players. The key to victory lies in your group's ability to adapt to the ever-present and always changing threats of prehistoric life. Should you focus on hunting and foraging to feed your starving tribe? Or should you be more concerned with supplying the dwindling fire with more wood? Perhaps constructing a weapon or tool might ease the stress of gathering resources... These choices and more await you in what will surely be the ultimate test of survival. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Phases 2.1 Day Phase 2.2 Night Phase 2.3 Morning Phase 3 Game End 4 Hindrance (Variant) Overview Don't Let It Die is essentially "RPG Skill Tree: The Game". As a team of four cavepeople, you must gather resources to stay alive--food, weapons, craftable items--while keeping the fire alive. The fire is how you gain FKP (fire knowledge points) or skill points that you use to improve your abilities, grow stronger, and survive. You have fifteen days to learn how to start your own fire, but if you die before then or the fire goes out due to lack of wood, the game is over. Phases Like most co-op games, the game alternates between "player actions" (day phase) and "bad things happen" (night phase). Day Phase Each character spends their turn taking actions, which cost stamina points. These are the basic actions. Some characters may have additional skills or abilities that alter actions. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] tl;dr The game is way too stacked against you to be fun and is poorly designed in almost every way.  Undeserving of the canned praise its getting from the high reviews.  A terrible Luck-based cluster-fest of chance and punishment.  A badly designed poor excuse for a Rogue-like at best, and most likely a predecessor to some half-cocked attempt at yet another idle mobile game.  The game has "replayability" only in how random the game is.  There is no strategy to speak of; if you gather and stockpile resources the randomness of the game will punish you for it.  Try and focus your efforts per char

[Rating: 2/10] The characters are cool. Also the main concept is okay.  But if you can survive or not, is completely random. No tactics, no decisions, only dice luck decides if you can move on or not.

[Rating: 2/10] Play Paleo instead  The only way to win is to accrue enough pips on a die roll fast enough.  The die has a "zero" on it.  Let that sink in...

[Rating: 3/10] tabletopia - very limited and random. If you know all the cards and events, you can plan better, but still no real challenge

[Rating: 4/10] Played via Tabletop Simulator. Interesting idea, bland execution. There's little sense of 'threat' right now, since the only ways to lose health are through random encounters or at the end of every night/day, meaning any 'danger' is predictable. The encounter decks are small enough that you'll see everything, so it's mostly a matter of letting time tick on and rolling the same die over and over to eventually reach your victory condition.

[Rating: 4/10] It could have been a good game. It's too close to Paleo. Paleo does the same thing but with a better story and is overall more immersive.
